headline: A distance appears inside a smallest carrier of the charge called four, produced by counting alone. Restrict the incidence table to one carrier's own sixteen pieces and join two pieces when no cutting among the 15800 uses both. The result is one of exactly two shapes and never anything else: the corners and edges of a four-cube on 60 of the 132 carriers, with 32 joins, and two separate three-cubes on the other 72, with 24 joins. Sixty and seventy-two make 132. The shape is constant on each of the six families of sizes 12, 12, 12, 24, 24 and 48, and the two join counts are the two values an earlier cycle recorded without naming. The shape then carries a distance and the table gives it back: one step apart is 0 shared cuttings by the way the joining is made, but two steps give 170 to 184, three steps give 240 to 250, and the far corner gives 433 every time, three bands that do not meet and that rise. Twelve counts occur in all and each belongs to one number of steps and no other, so the number of steps is a function of the count, and therefore does not depend on which relabelling the search returns. Inside a three-cube the far corner likewise gives one value, 250; pairs across the two cubes give 202 to 666, meeting none of the inside values, and the largest count in such a carrier is a crossing pair in 576 of 576 cases. The four-cube is not the ambient four-cube relabelled: a carrier's 5-corner cells cover all 16 corners of the object and joined pieces meet in exactly 2 corners, but 2016 farther pairs meet in 2 corners as well, so meeting in an edge is not what makes a join. A control of 768 evenly spaced sixteen-piece sets gives 0 of either shape against 132 of 132 for the carriers.
